name: Starter sequence
_doc: A shape to start from, not a script to send.
Every message in here is a gap in curly brackets rather than words. That is
deliberate and it is not an oversight. Check three of your send gate refuses
any message with a gap still in it, and says so: 'this still has {...} in it,
which is a gap nothing filled in. Write the words in yourself.' So this
sequence physically cannot send anything until you have replaced every gap
with your own words. Nothing of anybody else's goes out under your name by
accident, and you cannot approve your way past it.
The shape is the part worth copying. It is four ways a person can come back
from an opening message, and they are the four that actually happen. The
numbers underneath them come from 812 real conversations:
no reply at all        309 people   the biggest group by far
a pleasantry only      350 people   'thanks for connecting!' and nothing else
not now, or no          57 people
interested, asks back   42 people   the one you are doing all of it for
The lesson in those numbers is the one nobody expects. The largest group is
the people who said nothing, and almost nothing has ever been written for
them. The second largest said something that is not an answer. Most of the
work is in the two branches that feel like failures.
HOW IT IS WALKED. Each branch carries `steps`: what to do, which words, and how
long to wait, measured from the moment named in `from`. The engine reads these
as written. A due step is never sent by the engine in LinkChat - it is put in
your review queue, and it goes when you press approve. The words a step sends
live in `words` at the bottom, one entry per reference.
R0  the ladder for silence: your opener, ONE follow-up four days later, then
thirty quiet days and they are left alone. Two is the whole ladder.
R1  R2  R3  one reply each, due a few minutes after theirs arrives (the
engine picks a gap between four and eighteen minutes, so it never looks
like a machine answering on the second).
silence  a conversation that went quiet after you replied: one small nudge
three days on. If that is three days late it is skipped, not sent stale.

openers.label: Your opening message
openers.text: {your opening line - one or two sentences, in your own words, to somebody who has just connected with you}

branches.label: They are interested, or they ask you something back
branches.read: They wrote something that engages with what you said, or asked you a question. This is the one you built the sequence for. Answer the question first and completely, before anything else.
branches.next_move: {what you say to somebody who is genuinely interested - answer their question first, then one line about what happens next}
never: Never answer a question with a link and nothing else.
Never pitch in the same message that answers their question.

forward.then: send them the way to book time with you

branches.label: Not now, or no
branches.read: They have said no, or not at the moment. Take it at face value. The reply that keeps a door open is worth more than the one that argues.
branches.next_move: {what you say to somebody who has said no - short, no argument, leaves the door open}
never: Never send a second version of the same offer.

forward.then: make a note of the month they said

branches.label: A pleasantry, and nothing else
branches.read: 'Thanks for connecting!' or 'Great to be connected.' It reads like a reply and it answers nothing. 350 of 812 people landed here and six messages have ever been written for them. This is the biggest unworked group there is.
branches.next_move: {what you say to somebody who was only being polite - one question they can answer in a sentence, about them and not about you}
never: Never treat this as a yes.
Never send the same opener again in different words.

branches.label: No reply at all
branches.read: Four days and nothing. 309 of 812 people are standing here and NOT ONE message has ever gone out to them. That is the finding worth taking from this whole sequence: the largest group is the one nobody writes for, because it feels like a failure rather than a step.

steps.reason: two messages and thirty quiet days: left alone, on purpose

branches.next_move: {what you say to somebody who never replied - assume they never saw it, do not mention that they did not answer}
never: Never say 'just bumping this' or 'did you see my message'.
Never send a third one. Two is the whole ladder.

forward.then: stop here, and leave them alone

words.R0.f1: {your one follow-up to somebody who never replied - assume they never saw the first, do not mention that they did not answer}
words.R1.t1: {what you say to somebody who is genuinely interested - answer their question first, then one line about what happens next}
words.R2.t1: {what you say to somebody who has said no - short, no argument, leaves the door open}
words.R3.t1: {what you say to somebody who was only being polite - one question they can answer in a sentence, about them and not about you}
words.silence.step_1: {a small nudge to somebody who went quiet after you replied - two or three words, or a single emoji}
